title: PostgreSQL DBA Operational Playbook
description: Inspect active queries in pg_stat_activity, terminate runaway queries, diagnose lock contention, and check bloat.

data.text: When a production database experiences a CPU spike or latency stall, DBAs must quickly diagnose blocked locks and kill rogue queries using **`pg_stat_activity`** and cancellation functions.

data.title: Diagnosing and Terminating Runaway Queries
data.content: Viewing long-running queries and safely terminating them.
data.code:
-- 1. Find queries running for longer than 60 seconds
SELECT 
    pid,
    now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration,
    usename,
    state,
    query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state != 'idle'
  AND (now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start) > INTERVAL '60 seconds'
ORDER BY duration DESC;

-- 2. Gracefully cancel query (SIGINT - allows transaction rollback)
SELECT pg_cancel_backend(12345);

-- 3. Hard terminate backend connection if unresponsive (SIGTERM)
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(12345);

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `pg_stat_activity` gives real-time visibility into all connected clients and queries.
Set `statement_timeout = '30s'` in production to prevent runaway queries from hanging forever.
